title: Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ Advance to DARPA QBI Stage C
source_used: Quantum Computing Report (same DARPA announcement, read in full); HPCwire blocked (HTTP 403, Cloudflare)
key_facts: The US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) selected Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ to advance to Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI).
Stage C is the final verification phase: the assessment moves from paper R&D plans to direct physical testing of hardware, control electronics, cryogenic packaging and software decoders.

QBI asks whether commercial quantum computers can reach utility-scale operation by 2033; DARPA defines utility scale as the point where a system's computing output is worth more than its total capital and operating costs.
The four join Microsoft and PsiQuantum, the first pilot participants of the earlier programme, in Stage C.
Stage B was a yearlong assessment of R&D execution plans, risk mitigation models and prototype data.
DARPA's Independent Verification and Validation team will test the designs under long-term testing agreements; Micah Stoutimore, QBI Director at DARPA, manages the stage.
The article names the modality of each firm: neutral atoms (Atom Computing), silicon (Diraq) and trapped ions (IonQ); IBM's modality is not stated in the text.
quote_evidence: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has selected four commercial quantum hardware developers—Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM, and IonQ—to advance to Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI).

Stage C represents the final verification phase of DARPA’s evaluation framework, transitioning the assessment from theoretical R&D blueprint audits to direct physical testing, system measurement, and empirical validation of candidate fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) architectures.
why_it_matters_hint: A US defence agency moves four quantum hardware designs into physical testing; the 2033 utility-scale goal is DARPA's own target.
